description: AI capability K mapping: K = AI_score / human_expert_score, capped at 1.0

mmlu.note: Human expert performance reported in Hendrycks et al. 2021

usmle.note: Passed USMLE Step 1 & 2 at ~60% accuracy (Kung et al. 2023)
Expert-level on all USMLE steps (Nori et al. 2023)

bar_exam.note: ~60th-90th percentile on UBE; Martinez 2024 re-evaluation suggests 60th-69th, not 90th as OpenAI claimed

k_star_analysis.interpretation: K* = 0.85 is the critical capability threshold in our model where AI becomes 'good enough' that humans rationally delegate most tasks, triggering accelerated skill decay
findings: GPT-3.5 (K_avg=0.58): Well below K*. AI useful but clearly inferior to experts. Delegation partial.
GPT-4 (K_avg=0.86): Just crossed K*. First model where broad delegation becomes rational. This coincides with observed deskilling in Bastani et al. 2025.
GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 (K_avg=0.94): Well above K*. Near-expert across domains. Massive delegation incentive.
GPT-4.1+ (K_avg=0.96): Approaching ceiling. Human expertise increasingly redundant for delegated tasks.
Key insight: The GPT-3.5 -> GPT-4 jump (0.58 -> 0.86) crossed K* in ~12 months. This is the inflection point our model predicts as dangerous.
Caveat: GPT-4 bar exam '90th percentile' claim contested by Martinez 2024; likely 60th-69th. This doesn't change K_avg significantly.
Domain variation matters: coding K crossed threshold later than knowledge/reasoning K. This predicts domain-specific deskilling timelines.

timeline.pre_2023: K < 0.5 for most domains. AI as tool, not substitute.
timeline.2023_Q1: GPT-4 crosses K* (0.86). Rational delegation begins.
timeline.2024: GPT-4o/Claude 3.5 at K~0.94. Delegation near-universal for covered domains.
timeline.2025_plus: K approaching 1.0. The 'symbiosis trap' phase - maximum delegation, maximum deskilling risk.
